hub.title: Detection Tools | AICheck365
hub.description: AICheck365 tools: the AI Image & Video Detector on the homepage runs the one-click origin check, while the forensic tools below (C2PA Validator, C2PA Viewer, EXIF/XMP Reader, PNG Parameter Extractor, MP4 Metadata Inspector) inspect raw per-layer data locally in your browser.
hub.lead: Choose the evidence layer you need. Every file is parsed locally in your browser and is never uploaded.
hub.mainDesc: One-click checks for C2PA, EXIF, XMP, PNG text, MP4 metadata, file names, and sampled frame watermarks.

section.noScript: JavaScript is required to parse files locally; the explanatory content remains readable.

ui.sensitiveExport: The full export may include GPS, serial numbers, author contacts, prompts, workflow JSON, or other sensitive metadata. Continue?
ui.trustUnlisted: Signature valid, signer not trusted here
ui.problemUntrusted: Signer is not in the trust list

c2pa-validator.title: C2PA Validator | AICheck365
c2pa-validator.description: C2PA Validator: check whether a file carries a C2PA manifest and inspect signature state, claim generator, digital source type, assertions, ingredient chain, certificate info, and raw JSON. Analyzed locally, never uploaded.
c2pa-validator.lead: Upload an original image or video to inspect Content Credentials, signature validity, digital source type, claim generator, assertions, ingredient chain, certificate details, and validation issues.
c2pa-validator.uploadTitle: Upload a file to validate C2PA
c2pa-validator.uploadZone: Click or drag an image/video here
c2pa-validator.formats: JPEG / PNG / WebP / MP4 / MOV and more
usage: Use the closest available copy to the platform export.
Read signature state first, then digitalSourceType, claim_generator, and validation issues.
Copy or export raw JSON when you need an audit trail.
fields: Separates trusted, valid, invalid, and unsigned states.
Shows title, format, claim generator, digital source type, and assertions.
Displays issuer, signing time, algorithm, and upstream assets.
limits: No C2PA does not prove that a file is camera-made.
Exports, compression, screenshots, and transcoding can remove credentials.
A valid signature may still use a signer that is not in this engine’s trust list.
faq: Does no manifest mean the image is real?
No. It only means this copy has no readable C2PA manifest.
What is the difference between valid and trusted?
Both may be cryptographically valid; trusted additionally means the signer is in the active trust list.
Is the file uploaded?
No. Verification runs locally with WebAssembly.

c2pa-viewer.title: C2PA Viewer: Extract Raw Content Credentials JSON | AICheck365
c2pa-viewer.description: C2PA Viewer: inspect and extract raw C2PA manifests JSON locally in your browser. Copy or export raw Content Credentials without uploading files.
c2pa-viewer.lead: A distraction-free JSON view for developers and reviewers. Extract the C2PA manifest and search claim_generator, assertions, ingredients, certificates, and validation status.
c2pa-viewer.uploadTitle: Upload a file to extract C2PA JSON
c2pa-viewer.uploadZone: Click or drag an image/video here
c2pa-viewer.formats: JPEG / PNG / WebP / MP4 / MOV and more
usage: Choose the most original file available.
Search for claim_generator, digitalSourceType, assertions, or ingredients.
Copy or export the formatted JSON for debugging, auditing, or archiving.
fields: Displays the complete formatted JSON returned by the parser.
Preserves signature issues and state information.
Filter by field name or value.
limits: This page does not interpret evidence strength for you.
No manifest does not prove a file is human-made.
Exported JSON can contain certificate and provenance details.
faq: How is it different from the validator?
The viewer prioritizes raw JSON; the validator explains status and fields.
Can I copy the result?
Yes, copy or export formatted JSON.
Is the file uploaded?
No.

exif-xmp-reader.title: EXIF/XMP Reader: Inspect AI Image Metadata | AICheck365
exif-xmp-reader.description: EXIF/XMP Reader: inspect image EXIF, XMP, IPTC, base properties, and AI-tool fields locally in your browser, with searchable fields, safe copy, and JSON export.
exif-xmp-reader.lead: Read Software, CreatorTool, DigitalSourceType, AISystemUsed, timestamps, copyright, camera, and location fields, with AI-related and sensitive values clearly labeled.
exif-xmp-reader.uploadTitle: Upload an image to read EXIF / XMP
exif-xmp-reader.uploadZone: Click or drag an image here
exif-xmp-reader.formats: JPEG / PNG / WebP / GIF / BMP / TIFF
usage: Use an original image instead of a screenshot or social-media copy.
Search by software, platform, field name, or value.
Safe copy omits sensitive fields by default.
fields: Software, CreatorTool, DigitalSourceType, AISystemUsed, and similar values.
Dimensions, encoding, timestamp, Make, Model, and related properties.
GPS, serial numbers, contacts, UserComment, and prompts are labeled.
limits: EXIF/XMP can be edited, copied, or stripped.
No metadata does not mean an image is not AI-generated.
Review GPS and author information before a full export.
faq: Why is EXIF missing?
Screenshots, compression, forwarding, and re-exporting commonly remove metadata.
Does a Software field prove the source?
It is a clue, not a signature; combine it with C2PA and file provenance.
Is the file uploaded?
No.

png-parameter-extractor.title: ComfyUI Metadata Viewer: PNG Parameter Extractor | AICheck365
png-parameter-extractor.description: ComfyUI Metadata Viewer / PNG Parameter Extractor: read PNG tEXt, iTXt, zTXt, ComfyUI workflow, A1111 parameters, Stable Diffusion, and NovelAI metadata locally.
png-parameter-extractor.h1: ComfyUI Metadata Viewer and PNG Parameter Extractor
png-parameter-extractor.lead: Read ComfyUI prompt/workflow JSON, AUTOMATIC1111 parameters, Stable Diffusion settings, and NovelAI clues from PNG tEXt, iTXt, and zTXt chunks.
png-parameter-extractor.uploadTitle: Upload a PNG to extract parameters
png-parameter-extractor.uploadZone: Click or drag a PNG here
usage: Prefer a PNG exported directly by the generation tool.
Check for prompt, workflow, or parameters chunks.
Only export the full JSON when you need to reproduce or audit a workflow.
fields: Prompt, workflow, nodes, model, seed, sampler, and scheduler.
Positive and negative prompts, steps, CFG, size, model/hash.
Preserves each PNG text chunk and its source.
limits: PNG parameters are unsigned and can be edited.
Compression and screenshots usually remove text chunks.
Prompts and workflows may contain sensitive information.
faq: Is ComfyUI metadata EXIF?
Usually not. It is primarily stored in PNG text chunks and workflow JSON.
Is zTXt supported?
Yes, readable tEXt, iTXt, and zTXt chunks are supported.
Does no parameters mean it is not Stable Diffusion?
No. The data may have been stripped.

mp4-metadata-inspector.title: MP4/MOV Metadata Inspector: AI Video Container Fields | AICheck365
mp4-metadata-inspector.description: MP4/MOV Metadata Inspector: inspect MP4, MOV, and M4V brands, box tree, udta/meta/ilst fields, AIGC labels, SEI markers, and C2PA/JUMBF text clues locally.
mp4-metadata-inspector.lead: Start AI-video verification at the container layer: inspect ftyp brands, box tree, udta/meta/ilst, encoder fields, AIGC labels, platform strings, SEI markers, and C2PA/JUMBF clues.
mp4-metadata-inspector.uploadTitle: Upload a video to inspect container metadata
mp4-metadata-inspector.uploadZone: Click or drag an MP4 / MOV / M4V here
usage: Use the file downloaded directly from the generation platform.
Start with the summary and AI-related signals, then expand the box tree.
If the container is empty, use the main detector for sampled-frame analysis.
fields: Encoder, software, tool, comment, and AIGC fields.
Shows source paths, offsets, sizes, and recognized markers.
limits: Transcoding, editing, and social uploads often strip container fields.
No field does not prove that a video is human-made.
This page prioritizes the lightweight container pass and does not extract frames by default.
faq: How is this different from the homepage video detector?
This page focuses on MP4/MOV containers; the main detector can also sample frames.
Can it check Sora, Kling, or Runway?
It reports matching container fields, SEI markers, or platform strings that survive in the file.
Why not extract frames immediately?
Container inspection is faster and uses much less memory.
